findings.issue_text: Duplicate `downsize` method definition in app/models/optimized_image.rb: the newly added `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently shadows the updated 5-parameter version because Ruby does not support method overloading, leaving the 5-param method as unreachable dead code and breaking all pre-existing callers (e.g., thumbnail generation via OptimizedImage.create_for passing crop width/height positionally), which would raise ArgumentError (5 for 4) or bind the height Integer into opts causing a TypeError in optimize.

The downsize loop in app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-70 never checks the return value of OptimizedImage.downsize/convert_with, which returns false when ImageMagick exits non-zero (with stderr already discarded via `&> /dev/null`), so convert failures (missing binary, undecodable format, crash on a huge image) are silently swallowed and the code blindly proceeds to Upload.create_for anyway.

The downsize call writes output over input in place — `downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, …)` — destroying the user's only copy of the file; a convert that fails mid-write truncates the tempfile, and an empty/corrupt file is then handed to upload creation with no indication that downsizing failed.

ImageMagick picks the output format from the output filename's extension, but tempfile.path has no extension, so even a successful downsize depends on ImageMagick's input-format fallback for an extensionless output.

The animated-GIF branch can never trigger in the new code path: `optimize` selects the _animated instruction set only when the source path ends in .gif, but the controller passes an extensionless tempfile.path, so `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is dead code in this path and oversized animated GIFs are resized with the non-animated instructions (without -coalesce), producing glitched/corrupted animations due to the two extension checks using different inputs (original filename vs. tempfile path).

No verification that the file is actually under the limit when the downsize loop exits: the loop is hard-capped at 5 passes of 80% and byte size does not track pixel count (PNGs and already-compressed JPEGs frequently don't shrink proportionally), so a still-oversized file falls straight through to Upload.create_for with no check, no fallback, and no specific error, silently failing the feature's contract and potentially bypassing the configured max_image_size_kb limit.

Client-side upload limit in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js is hardcoded to 10MB, decoupled from site settings: validateUploadedFiles previously enforced max_<type>_size_kb per upload type but now allows any file up to 10MB, so oversized attachments are no longer caught client-side, the server error handler always claims the max is 10MB (wrong for attachments and for deployments with client_max_body_size below 10MB), and sites that raised max_image_size_kb above 10MB can no longer receive images between 10MB and their configured limit.

`rescue nil` on `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, …)` in app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb masks why the URL download failed (bad URL, over the cap), and execution falls through to `tempfile.size` on nil, raising NoMethodError and returning an opaque 500 instead of a meaningful error.
The URL download cap is hardcoded to 10.megabytes, decoupling the API download limit from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, so sites that raised the setting still cannot URL-fetch larger images.

Duplicate `def self.downsize` in app/models/optimized_image.rb — the PR adds a second definition (from, to, dimensions, opts={}) directly below the existing (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}); Ruby has no method overloading, so the second silently replaces the first, leaving the 4/5-arg version as dead code and breaking un-updated callers: 5-arg calls raise ArgumentError (5 for 3..4) and 4-arg calls bind height into opts so opts[:allow_animation] raises TypeError, breaking animated thumbnail generation (the animated-GIF branch of OptimizedImage.create_for) and any width/height-style caller including plugins.

The downsize loop in uploads_controller.rb runs up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick passes before any server-side size/dimension validation — the only 10MB gate is client-side JS (trivially bypassed via direct POST/API) and the multipart path has no cap before ImageMagick is invoked, so a decompression-bomb image can request a multi-GB pixel cache (IM6 has no default area/dimension cap), causing memory/disk exhaustion amplified by 5 iterations per upload and concurrent uploads inside request threads (worker saturation / DoS by any authenticated user).

The failure return of OptimizedImage.downsize / convert_with is never checked in the controller loop, so failures are silently ignored — even a corrupt or bogus 'image' forces all 5 ImageMagick spawns before rejection, and the loop can silently no-op 5 times.

OptimizedImage.downsize is called in-place with tempfile.path as both source and destination, but Rack multipart / FileHelper.download tempfiles have no file extension — ImageMagick selects the output coder from the destination filename's extension, so convert typically fails with 'no encode delegate for this image format', leaving the downsize feature dead on arrival.
On a partial-write failure, the in-place convert operation destroys the original tempfile mid-write, leaving a truncated file that Upload.create_for may then accept and store.

The 5×80% iterative downsize loop cannot converge in common configurations — 0.8^5 ≈ 0.33, so any image more than ~3× the configured limit (e.g., sites with max_image_size_kb of 1-2MB against the new 10MB client allowance) burns all 5 full decode/re-encode passes and then rejects the upload anyway; PNGs are worse since ImageMagick's -quality for PNG controls lossless compression, not file size, so shrinking dimensions doesn't guarantee dropping under the limit — a single-pass approach (compute the target scale once, or -define jpeg:extent=<limit> for JPEG) would be O(1) re-encodes instead of O(5).

Client-side upload limit hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js instead of reading SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] — sites with max_attachment_size_kb or max_image_size_kb above 10MB can no longer receive those uploads (client blocks what the server accepts), the 413 handler always claims the max is 10MB even when the real nginx/app limit differs (misleading errors), and future site-setting changes silently break the client check; the same hardcode is applied to the API URL-download cap (uploads_controller.rb:55).

The animated-GIF branch can never trigger for uploads — optimize only selects *_instructions_animated when the source path matches /\.GIF$/i, but multipart and FileHelper.download tempfile paths are extensionless, so the allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails argument is dead code in this call path and animated GIFs above the limit fall through to the static instructions, where resizing a disposal-optimized GIF without -coalesce corrupts frames / drops the animation.
allow_animated_thumbnails is a thumbnail setting being semantically misused to decide whether user uploads keep their animation.

The downsize block ignores `type` — create_upload handles both image and attachment, but the block only checks FileHelper.is_image?(filename), so an image posted as an attachment (governed by max_attachment_size_kb) is downsized against max_image_size_kb, silently degrading full-resolution files the user intended to attach as-is.

Duplicate `downsize` definition in app/models/optimized_image.rb:146-152 — the second 3-arg definition silently shadows the 4-arg version, making it dead code and causing existing 4-arg callers to raise TypeError (Integer bound to opts) or ArgumentError, breaking thumbnail generation

Retry loop in app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66-69 ignores the false return value from `convert_with` when the convert subprocess fails, spawning 5 doomed convert processes per upload for corrupt/unsupported images and proceeding with the untouched file as if nothing happened

Bounded retry (5 passes at 80% scale) in uploads_controller.rb:63-71 is not tied to the goal of reaching max_image_size_kb — encoded size doesn't track dimensions, and on exhaustion the code silently falls through to Upload.create_for with no post-loop check or distinct error for failure to converge

Client-side upload limit hardcoded to 10MB in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182, decoupled from max_image_size_kb/max_attachment_size_kb site settings — >10MB attachments are hard-blocked with no workaround and admins cannot effectively raise limits past 10MB

`allow_animation` option is dead code on the downsize path — the animated branch in `optimize` requires `from` to match /\.GIF$/i but tempfile.path has no .gif extension, so animated GIFs are processed with static-image instructions that can mangle the animation, and a thumbnail setting now decides whether original uploads keep animation

No server-side 10MB ceiling before the downsize loop in uploads_controller.rb:63-71 — the client-side check is bypassable via API and direct multipart requests, allowing images of any size to trigger up to 5 synchronous convert runs on the full-size file

In-place downsize in uploads_controller.rb:67 — `convert` writes output directly onto its own input tempfile, so a failed or killed command can leave the only copy of the upload truncated or corrupt, which may then pass the size check and be passed to Upload.create_for damaged

No wall-clock timeout on `convert` in optimized_image.rb:161-163 — the new call path runs up to 5 sequential blocking subprocesses on user-supplied images inside the HTTP request, so a decompression/pixel bomb under 10MB can pin or OOM a unicorn worker indefinitely

413 handler in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 always reports '10MB' as the limit even when the 413 originates from a proxy client_max_body_size or a per-type server setting, giving users incorrect information about the actual constraint

Extension-less API URLs never get downsized — in uploads_controller.rb:55-56, URLs without an image extension (e.g., .../getimage?id=3) fail FileHelper.is_image?, so oversized images fetched that way are rejected while the identical image via multipart or a .jpg URL succeeds, producing inconsistent behavior

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

The diff doesn’t show whether `Upload.create_for` will reliably reject an oversized/failed-to-downsize image, so the impact as a definite correctness bug isn’t fully verifiable here, but the lack of failure handling is a concrete review issue introduced by this change.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, passing the same path as both input and output. In `optimized_image.rb`, `convert_with` executes an external convert command writing to `to` and returns `false` on failure, but the controller ignores the return value and proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` regardless. The diff therefore clearly introduces an in-place rewrite with no error handling; if the conversion fails or produces a bad file, the tempfile can be left corrupt/empty and still uploaded.

adjudication.rationale: The new upload resizing loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` in `uploads_controller.rb`, using the same Tempfile path for input and output. A Tempfile path commonly has no image extension, and the ImageMagick command constructed by `OptimizedImage` relies on the `to` filename to determine output format. Since `to` is extensionless here, the output format selection can be ambiguous or fail depending on ImageMagick defaults, making the downsize behavior potentially broken for large images.

adjudication.rationale: In the new controller path, oversized images are downsized via `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` (uploads_controller.rb). In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, the animated branch is selected only if `opts[:allow_animation]` is true *and* `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` (optimized_image.rb). Here `from` is `tempfile.path`, which is commonly an extensionless temp file path, while the image check uses `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` based on the original filename. This mismatch means animated GIFs can be processed with non-animated instructions (no `-coalesce`), potentially corrupting animations, making `allow_animation` ineffective for this code path.

The finding’s broader claims about “silently failing” or “bypassing” the configured limit aren’t verifiable from this diff (since `Upload.create_for` validations aren’t shown), but the missing post-loop verification/handling is a concrete, diff-grounded edge case.

adjudication.rationale: In `create_upload`, when `file.nil? && url.present? && is_api?`, `tempfile = FileHelper.download(...) rescue nil` can set `tempfile` to `nil`. Although the newly added downsize block guards with `if tempfile && ...`, the method still unconditionally calls `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...)`, which will raise `NoMethodError` on `tempfile.size` if the download failed. In `optimized_image.rb`, `convert_with` returns `false` when the ImageMagick command fails, and that result propagates up through `optimize`/`downsize`, but the controller ignores it. If conversion fails (e.g., corrupt/bogus image or ImageMagick error), `tempfile.size` will likely remain > limit, so the loop can spawn up to 5 failing ImageMagick processes and then proceed anyway, effectively ignoring the failure signal.

From the diff, the destination is purely `tempfile.path` (not derived from `filename`), so any extension present on `filename` is not used for the output name. This makes it likely the output path has no image extension (common for Rack/Tempfile and `FileHelper.download` tempfiles), which can cause ImageMagick to fail to select an output format when writing, breaking the intended “auto-reduce then upload” behavior.

In `optimized_image.rb`, `allow_animation` directly controls whether `*_instructions_animated` is used for GIFs, so when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is false, downsizing a large animated GIF will use the non-animated instructions and can strip animation. That ties upload animation preservation to a thumbnail-related setting, plausibly causing incorrect/broken behavior for user uploads.

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the new downsize loop triggers solely on `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` and `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, without considering the `type` argument. Since the same method handles multiple upload types (passed in as `type`), an image uploaded under a non-image type (e.g. an attachment) would still be recompressed/downsized to satisfy `max_image_size_kb`, potentially degrading an attachment that should instead be governed by its own size limit (e.g. `max_attachment_size_kb`). This is a behavior-changing, silent data-quality loss risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate `downsize` definition in app/models/optimized_image.rb:146-152 — the second 3-arg definition silently shadows the 4-arg version, making it dead code and causing existing 4-arg callers to raise TypeError (Integer bound to opts) or ArgumentError, breaking thumbnail generation

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/optimized_image.rb`, the diff leaves an updated 5-arg `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and then introduces a new `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` below it. In Ruby the later definition overwrites the earlier one, so existing callers passing 4 args (e.g. `downsize(from,to,w,h)`) will now bind `dimensions=w` and `opts=h` (an Integer), and `optimize` will treat `opts` like a Hash (`opts[:allow_animation]`), causing runtime errors / broken image resizing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Retry loop in app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66-69 ignores the false return value from `convert_with` when the convert subprocess fails, spawning 5 doomed convert processes per upload for corrupt/unsupported images and proceeding with the untouched file as if nothing happened

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new retry loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times but never checks its return value. In optimized_image.rb, `convert_with` returns `false` when the convert subprocess fails (non-zero exit), and `optimize` returns that value, so `downsize` can fail. If it fails, `tempfile.size` likely remains unchanged, making the loop condition (`tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`) stay true and spawning up to 5 failing convert attempts before proceeding with the original, unmodified file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Bounded retry (5 passes at 80% scale) in uploads_controller.rb:63-71 is not tied to the goal of reaching max_image_size_kb — encoded size doesn't track dimensions, and on exhaustion the code silently falls through to Upload.create_for with no post-loop check or distinct error for failure to converge

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in `uploads_controller.rb` does attempt to reach `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` by looping while `tempfile.size > ...` (so it is tied to the goal), but the reviewer concern about the bounded retry and lack of an explicit post-loop failure handling is grounded: after 5 iterations it can still be oversized and the code unconditionally proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` with no explicit check or dedicated error path in this method. Whether `Upload.create_for` rejects oversized files (and how it reports that) is not shown in the diff, so it’s not a verifiable defect from the diff alone, but it is a concrete edge-case/UX correctness concern introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side upload limit hardcoded to 10MB in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182, decoupled from max_image_size_kb/max_attachment_size_kb site settings — >10MB attachments are hard-blocked with no workaround and admins cannot effectively raise limits past 10MB

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the per-type site setting lookup (`Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`) and `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` in `utilities.js`. The client-side check returns `false` when `fileSizeKB > maxSizeKB`, so uploads >10MB are blocked in the browser regardless of admin-configured `max_*_size_kb` settings, creating a settings-ignoring regression as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `allow_animation` option is dead code on the downsize path — the animated branch in `optimize` requires `from` to match /\.GIF$/i but tempfile.path has no .gif extension, so animated GIFs are processed with static-image instructions that can mangle the animation, and a thumbnail setting now decides whether original uploads keep animation

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new auto-reduction loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. In `optimized_image.rb`, `optimize` only selects the `_animated` instructions when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true **and** `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. But `from` here is `tempfile.path` (a temp filename), and in the URL-download path the tempfile is created with prefix `"discourse-upload-#{type}"` (no `.gif` extension). So even for an animated GIF upload, the animated branch can be skipped and static instructions used, which can destroy animation. Also, the choice to preserve animation for original uploads is now tied to `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`, as shown by the new call site.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No server-side 10MB ceiling before the downsize loop in uploads_controller.rb:63-71 — the client-side check is bypassable via API and direct multipart requests, allowing images of any size to trigger up to 5 synchronous convert runs on the full-size file

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb, the new pre-Upload.create_for downsize loop runs synchronously on the uploaded tempfile whenever it’s an image and exceeds SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, with up to 5 OptimizedImage.downsize(convert) runs. For multipart uploads (file present), there is no explicit server-side upper bound (like 10MB) before entering this loop; the only new 10MB limit in the diff is for API URL downloads (FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)). Thus a client-side size check (also changed to a hardcoded 10MB) is bypassable for direct multipart requests, allowing very large images to trigger repeated expensive processing before any later validation/rejection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In-place downsize in uploads_controller.rb:67 — `convert` writes output directly onto its own input tempfile, so a failed or killed command can leave the only copy of the upload truncated or corrupt, which may then pass the size check and be passed to Upload.create_for damaged

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in `uploads_controller.rb` downsizes images by calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, i.e., using the same path for input and output. `OptimizedImage` ultimately shells out in `convert_with` to perform the conversion, with no temporary output file / atomic rename and no return-value handling in the controller. If the external convert process fails mid-write (or otherwise produces a partial/invalid file when overwriting), the only copy (`tempfile`) can be left corrupted/truncated; the loop condition then relies on `tempfile.size` and could stop once the file becomes small enough, proceeding to `Upload.create_for(...)` with a damaged file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No wall-clock timeout on `convert` in optimized_image.rb:161-163 — the new call path runs up to 5 sequential blocking subprocesses on user-supplied images inside the HTTP request, so a decompression/pixel bomb under 10MB can pin or OOM a unicorn worker indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new in-request loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that can call `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times on a user-supplied image (`while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`). In `optimized_image.rb`, `convert_with` runs ImageMagick via backticks (``#{instructions.join(" ")} &> /dev/null``) with no wall-clock timeout or resource limits shown in the diff. That means a crafted image (e.g., decompression/pixel bomb within the 10MB download cap) could cause long-running/CPU- or memory-intensive `convert` executions, potentially tying up the request worker, and the new loop amplifies this risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 413 handler in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 always reports '10MB' as the limit even when the 413 originates from a proxy client_max_body_size or a per-type server setting, giving users incorrect information about the actual constraint

adjudication.rationale: The diff hard-codes the 413 error message limit in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js` from `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to `10 * 1024` (10MB). Since a 413 can be caused by upstream/proxy limits or different per-type limits, this change can make the UI always report 10MB even when the actual enforced limit differs, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Extension-less API URLs never get downsized — in uploads_controller.rb:55-56, URLs without an image extension (e.g., .../getimage?id=3) fail FileHelper.is_image?, so oversized images fetched that way are rejected while the identical image via multipart or a .jpg URL succeeds, producing inconsistent behavior

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing block in `uploads_controller.rb` is guarded by `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`, but for API URL uploads `filename` is derived from `File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)`. If the URL path has no image extension (e.g. `/getimage`), `filename` will be extension-less, so this guard can prevent downsizing from running for an actual image response. That creates inconsistent behavior vs multipart uploads (which typically include an image filename), and can cause oversized images from such URLs to remain oversized and then be rejected by later size validations in `Upload.create_for`.
